description: issue #681 (slice I2), the NUMBER half of the number-vs-word rule: `spec/interaction-events.md:136-137` — "If the submitted text parses as an OpenLogo number literal, the reporter returns a number." The scripted answer is the TEXT "42" (the raw characters a learner would type), and the read reports the NUMBER 42, proven by arithmetic rather than by printed text: `:answer + 1` prints 43, which only a number can do — the word "42" would raise `ol-type` instead. Pair with `input-word-answer`, which scripts a non-numeral through the identical program shape. Per the maintainer's #657 ruling `input` is tested by MOCKING the answer through `executeOptions.hostInput.responses` (a FIFO consumed in order by each `input` call), and the read introduces NO new event kind: it emits the ordinary catch-all `primitive` event named `input` (`spec/interaction-events.md:105-106`) AFTER the read finishes, so `spec/execution-model.md`'s trace/event registry is unchanged. The payload carries only `name` — never the prompt or the submitted text — and no `turtle-id`, because a read concerns no turtle.
